text:
alex: seeing a spike of 503s from eu-west for our hosted endpoints after the cert rollover earlier. only affects clients coming from our NAT egress (shared NATs), not from direct VPC peering.

marta: same. customer-reported. traces show ALB 503 with `GetConnection` errors right at TLS handshake.

jordan: any pattern on SNI? wildcard vs exact?

alex: looks like ALB listener is matching wildcard rule for `*.service.redwood` and forwarding to TLS-termination target group. but some clientHello samples show `alpn` only contains `h2` (no http/1.1) and ALB rejects -> 503. also saw client_hello SNI `service.eu-west-01` (exact) but matching rule appears to be wildcard which has different cert chain.

kevin: deploy-bot posted a cert rotation event at 1767543000 for `wildcard.service.redwood` - might be correlated. deploy-bot: "cert-rotation: wildcard.service.redwood rotated, pushed to secret-store, rollout to ingress-controller started" :deploy:

infra-bot: autoscaler triggered scale-down of gpu-inference-pool at 1767542850, several ingress-controller pods rescheduled to other nodes (some moved across AZs).

marta: could the ingress reload have been mid-rotation and briefly served an incomplete cert bundle? I saw `certificate not configured` in one kube-proxy log.

alex: attaching a short snippet of ALB logs we have:
```
type: "request" elb_status_code: 503 target_status_code: -1 tls_ver: TLSv1.3 client_ip: 52.30.12.45 sni: service.eu-west-01 alpn: h2 tls_alert: handshake_failure
```

jordan: hm. two hypotheses: (1) ALB listener priority/order makes wildcard rule take precedence when client uses SNI exact; rotation changed cert metadata so ALB considered cert invalid for that rule. (2) ingress TLS termination race: ingress-controller restarted and didn't have secret until sidecar reloaded -> ALB sees no cert and fails handshake.

kevin: quick check: can we confirm if the ingress-controller pods had the updated secret mount before the ALB health check? kube-events show `Secret updated` at 1767542995 and ingress pod restarts at 1767543030. that suggests the reload happened after cert push.

marta: also noticed NAT egress IPs map to a different egress CLB we recently enabled for cost reasons in eu-west. that CLB is configured with TCP pass-through to NLB -> we might have double-terminate attempts?

alex: what if some clients are doing mTLS (mutual TLS) and the ALB is not configured for client cert request on wildcard rule? some customers do mTLS over dedicated endpoints. we should check listener config.

jordan: checking listener rules now:
```
Listener 443: 
 - Rule 1 priority 1: Host header exact `service.eu-west-01.redwood` -> HTTPS target group TLS-terminate (cert: exact) -> target port 8443
 - Rule 2 priority 5: Host header wildcard `*.service.redwood` -> HTTPS target group TLS-terminate (cert: wildcard)
```
If ALB picks rule 2 for some reason, you get wildcard cert. If the wildcard cert bundle was rotated and missing intermediate chain, client with strict verification may fail.

kevin: intermediate was present in secret-store but the cert-loader sidecar has a bug where it streams content and occasionally truncates the pem on restart. we have two incidents logged earlier this month.

marta: suggested immediate mitigations?

alex: quick fixes: (A) re-prioritize exact host rule above wildcard (low risk), (B) temporarily route eu-west NAT egress IPs to fallback LB that uses older cert, (C) force restart of ingress pods sequentially after verifying full PEM.

sre-oncall: I'll run (A) now and monitor. also enabling ALB access logging for the period.

sre-oncall: done. moved exact rule to priority 1 explicitly and flushed ALB rule cache. watch dashboard. :eyes:

infra-bot: ALB access logs enabled for loadbalancer/app/edge-eu-west at 1767543400.

alex: after the change, customer 123's requests started succeeding within 30s. still seeing a small tail of failures from the shared NAT pool.

kevin: I'm going to rollback the cert-loader change and deploy a fix that validates full PEM length before writing. scheduling a rolling update to ingress-controller with a pre-check of the secret contents.

marta: also filing a follow-up to add explicit SNI-to-rule telemetry to the tracing so we can see which rule matched on a per-request basis.

jordan: long-term: consider NLB passthrough + KTLS on pod side for mTLS customers, or use dedicated endpoints for mTLS traffic to avoid wildcard mismatches. makes cost vs complexity tradeoff.

alex: yep. logging this for postmortem: root cause likely cert-loader truncation + ALB rule ordering + egress path changes exposing strict clients. impact: intermittent 503s for NAT egressed traffic in eu-west for ~18min. customers affected: small set on mTLS strict mode.

kevin: I'll push a hotfix and a cert-loader canary to one AZ and watch.

marta: thanks. can we add a runbook step to check `kubectl get secrets -n ingress` and `kubectl logs` for `cert-loader` before doing rotations?

alex: agreed. adding runbook note and assigning to infra runbook repo.

jordan: closing loop: prod alert cleared at 1767544300. last failure sample at 1767544282.

sre-oncall: monitoring for 1 hour, will escalate if reappears. :thumbsup:
